title: 将Ctrl+c 的复制功能映射到一个键盘按键后，按这个键第二次，复制的文本内容还是第一次的文本内容

status.label: Validate repeated Ctrl+C remapping
status.detail: The reporter gives a concrete Scroll Lock-to-Ctrl+C sequence on PowerToys 0.85.1, including stale clipboard contents and Ctrl remaining pressed; current-build behavior is unknown.

judgment.rationale: The report specifies a Scroll Lock-to-Ctrl+C mapping and two repeated activations: the second copy reportedly retains the first selection, and Ctrl remains pressed. This is a focused maintainer reproduction, but it is reported only on PowerToys 0.85.1 and there is no evidence it persists on a supported build. Reproduce the same sequence locally before designing a code change.
evidence: The issue reports PowerToys 0.85.1 and maps Ctrl+C to Scroll Lock.
The reporter says the second activation copies the first selection instead of the newly selected text.
The reporter separately says Ctrl can remain pressed after repeated activation.
The issue is open, has no comments, and has no assignee.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the exact repeated-selection sequence on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer in a disposable text buffer and verify both clipboard contents and modifier release.

fix_assessment.rationale: The only reported build is 0.85.1 and the issue does not establish whether the two symptoms persist today. A current-build maintainer reproduction is available; no specific code correction is justified until that result isolates a still-failing path.

issue_context.summary: Repeated Scroll Lock-to-Ctrl+C remaps reportedly copy stale text and can leave Ctrl pressed.
known_information: The source key is Scroll Lock and the target shortcut is Ctrl+C.
The reporter describes stale clipboard content on the second activation and a Ctrl modifier that remains pressed.
inferences: The paired symptoms may involve repeated injected shortcut events or modifier state, but the report does not identify which event or release path fails.
issue_context.analysis: The issue provides enough detail for a maintainer-controlled test without asking for generic logs. Use distinct text selections and a disposable editor so the clipboard result and any stuck modifier can be observed independently on a current build.
initial_investigation: Read the complete Chinese issue body; there are no later comments, assignees, or current-build retest.
Separated the stale-copy symptom from the reported stuck-Ctrl symptom so each can be checked in the same controlled sequence.

actions.label: Reproduce repeated Ctrl+C remapping
actions.note: The report has a specific sequence; verify whether either symptom remains on a current build before proposing a code change.

reproduce.title: Verify repeated Scroll Lock-to-Ctrl+C remaps
prerequisites: A text editor with a disposable buffer
setup: Map Scroll Lock to Ctrl+C in Keyboard Manager.
Open a disposable text buffer and prepare two different strings, such as alpha and beta.
steps: Select alpha and press Scroll Lock; verify the clipboard contains alpha.
Select beta and press Scroll Lock again; paste into a separate line and verify the clipboard contains beta.
Release Scroll Lock, focus an empty line, and type an ordinary letter to check whether Ctrl remains logically pressed.
reproduce.expected_result: Each activation should copy the current selection, and Ctrl should be released after the remapped key is released.
